THO.
DEPARTMENT OF THE ARMY 
OFFICE OF THE CHIEF OF ENGINEERS WASHINGTON, D.C. 20314
IN REPLY REFER TO
ENGCW-PV
19 May 19/1
Honorable Charles J. Orlebete
Deputy Under Secretary
Department of Housing and Urban
Development
Washington, D. C. 20410
Dear Mr. Orlebeke:
This responds to your 9 April 1971 request for comments on the draft environmental statement on Operation Breakthrough. We offer our compliments on what certainly appears to be a commendable program. This is an excellent example of the interdisciplinary application of technology, and we wish you every success in your efforts to meet the Nation's housing needs in a more rational manner.
Our review indicates that Operation Breakthrough would not appear to adversely affect programs administered by the Corps of Engineers. We presume, however, that an environmental statement would be developed to cover the specifics of each site prior to the time construction is to be initiated.
The following comments are offered to assist in preparing your final environmental statement:
The proposed breakthrough program is oriented to "housing systems as alternatives to conventional living arrangements in residential communities." The program should consider and discuss how the mass produced product can live in harmony with these already existing residential communities. One of the great advantages of the Operation Breakthrough program industrialized building systems is their speed. Care must be exercised so that the impetus of the systems does not create the wholesale destruction of the character and sense of place of our cities.
